title: fix(metadata-protocol): a seed that stores many seedFile values no longer starves sign-ins (yield per row, 20-row batches)
body:
Fixes #26670

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:种子加载器在每一行种子文件的存储与认领之后各让出一次事件循环;携带种子文件的数据集改为每批 20 行插入(原为 200 行)。无种子文件的数据集行为不变。
- **为什么改**:实测证伪了卡上「连接池被占用」的推测——连接池最长持有 44 ms;真正被占住的是事件循环:同步的 sqlite 驱动让每个 await 都成了微任务,一批 200 行的认领连成一条不间断的链,开机种子期间的登录请求要等 3–5 秒才被读到。
- **风险与回滚**:风险低,只改变种子文件工作的调度顺序,不改写入内容与结果;回滚即撤销本 PR 的两个 fix 提交。
- **先看**:`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-files.ts`(`yieldToEventLoop` 及两处调用点,`settleRow` 的 `finally`);`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`(`insertBatchSize`)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/seed-loader-seed-files.test.ts`,预期 19 passed,其中「a seed of many files yields to waiting requests (#26670)」三条全绿。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**The reading first: which call holds what.** The card's seam ("the seed loader holds a pooled connection or a transaction") was marked unverified, so the first measurement was the pool itself. No call on the seed-file path opens a transaction: none in `seed-loader.ts`, `seed-files.ts` or `field-file-service.ts`, nor in the boot runner (`app-plugin.ts` `runInlineSeed`). Every step is sequential, and there is no `Promise.all`. Measured on the real composition (`os serve --dev`, file-backed sqlite, 1,500 rows each holding one 20 KB `seedFile`, sign-in every 250 ms while the background seed runs). A preload patched tarn's `Pool` (acquire, release) and sampled event-loop lag with a 100 ms timer:

| reading | before (base `a485b5a3`) | after (fix at `abc4ef3b`; `src` unchanged since) |
|---|---|---|
| pool acquires during the run | 37,494 | 38,430 |
| longest connection hold | 44 ms | 103 ms |
| longest acquire wait | 21 ms | 19 ms |
| event-loop lag, max per 5 s window, during the seed | 2,827–4,996 ms | 170–317 ms |
| sign-ins during the seed: p50 / slowest | 358 ms / 5,195 ms | 187 ms / 447 ms |

The pool was never starved. The **event loop** was. On a synchronous driver (better-sqlite3) every `await` of a seed file's roughly 25 engine calls (the `pending` `sys_file` row, the bytes, then `claimFiles`: describe, `ownedBySlot`, release, commit, each with its write hooks and audit rows) resolves as a microtask. The loader buffers inserts into 200-row batches, and after each flush `settleSeedFiles` claims the batch's rows back to back. Those claims involve no I/O at all, so a whole batch ran as one unbroken microtask chain, and a sign-in arriving meanwhile was not even read off the socket until it ended. The stalls landed once per batch (about 8 for 1,500 rows), and a CPU profile put the time in better-sqlite3's synchronous `_query` and `prepare`. Control on the same boot without file values: 1,500 rows and also 30,000 rows finish inside the 8 s inline budget, with about 2,140 acquires in all, so the cost is the per-row file work and not row count.

**The fix**, in the producer (`packages/metadata-protocol`, inside the claim's file surface):

1. `seed-files.ts` gets `yieldToEventLoop()`, one `setImmediate` turn. This is the cure `@objectstack/core`'s import runner already applies to the same trap. `prepareRow` ends with it when the row stored or kept files, and `settleRow` ends with it (in a `finally`) after every row's claim. A request now waits behind one row's files, never behind a batch's.
2. `seed-loader.ts` writes a dataset that carries seed files (`SeedDatasetFiles.carriesFiles`, the bundled `files` map is non-empty) in insert batches of `SEED_FILE_BATCH_SIZE = 20` instead of 200. With the settle loop broken up, the remaining stall was the single `insertMany` of 200 file-bearing rows: about 1.5 s, since each row's file-reference hooks cost about 7 ms on sqlite. At 20 rows that is about 150 ms. Datasets without seed files keep the 200-row batch.

⛔ No pool size or timeout was raised. The seed's wall time is unchanged within boot noise (about 25–30 s of seed in each 1,500-file run).

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` and `packages/services/service-storage/src/field-file-service.ts` are untouched: neither holds anything.

## Tests

New `describe` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-seed-files.test.ts`. It seeds 60 files on an object with no self-reference, so the loader takes the batched-insert path the stall was measured on. The suite's fake engine and field-file service resolve purely in microtasks, which is the property of better-sqlite3 that matters, so the pin is deterministic without a driver:

- `stores at most one row's files and settles at most one row's claim between two macrotask turns`: samples progress on every `setImmediate` turn while the load runs.
- `serves an unrelated read issued during the seed within one row's file work`: a `sys_user` read issued from a macrotask, standing in for the sign-in's user lookup.
- `writes a dataset that carries seed files in insert batches of at most 20 rows`.

Ablations (each mutation landed and restored by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor and blob counts and proves the restore against the HEAD blob; the test imports source, so no `dist/` is involved):

- **A**: `yieldToEventLoop` resolves at once. Pins 1 and 2 red: `no macrotask turn ran while the seed ran: expected 0 to be greater than 1`, `the read never completed: expected undefined to be defined`. 2 failed, 17 passed.
- **B**: `SEED_FILE_BATCH_SIZE = 200`. Pin 3 red: `expected 60 to be less than or equal to 20`. 1 failed, 18 passed.
- **C**: only the settle-side yield removed. Pin 1 red: `expected { maxStored: 1, maxClaims: 20 } to deeply equal { maxStored: 1, maxClaims: 1 }`, which is a whole batch's claims settled with no turn, the measured shape. The first attempt at C was a no-op (the tool refused: the replacement was a substring of its anchor, so the test never ran); it was re-run with a distinct replacement.
- A first version of the pins seeded `clm_version`, whose self-lookup sends the loader down the sequential per-record path. Leg B stayed green against it, which exposed the pins as vacuous for the batched path. They were moved to `clm_doc` before the legs above.

Runs on the final head `4bf7600183` unless noted:

<details><summary>Readings</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/seed-loader-seed-files.test.ts` at `4bf7600183`: `Tests  19 passed (19)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck` at `4bf7600183`: exit 0 (same `&&` chain). The test file is in the tsc program (`--listFiles` names it once).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` at `d294c889` (the merge of `origin/main`; the only later commit types one test literal): `Test Files  269 passed | 3 skipped (272)`, `Tests  21619 passed | 19 skipped (21638)`, after rebuilding the package's dependency closure (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/metadata-protocol^...' build`).
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the three changed source files: exit 0.
- Boot measurement: scratch scripts, not committed; numbers in the table above.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Not reproduced here:** the card's `Knex: Timeout acquiring a connection` refusal. The measured pool waits never exceeded 21 ms, so this run shows the sign-in *slowdown* (5.2 s at worst on 1,500 small files) and its cause, not the refusal. hotclm's 28 s sign-in and its refusals are consistent with longer per-batch stalls (bigger files, more write hooks), but that is inference, not a reading.
- **A residual stall at the end of the seed, outside this diff:** one 3.3 s event-loop stall as the seed settles (a sign-in took 3,548 ms then). The profile slice shows `emitSeedSettled`, then `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle`, then `claimSeedOwnership` (`@objectstack/plugin-security`, the ADR-0138 hand-over on `app:seeded`), with a driver `updateMany` and per-row insert and audit frames. It re-owns the seeded rows in one unbroken chain, scales with rows rather than files, and runs for any seed that overruns the inline budget. Reported to the seat, not fixed here.
- The boot measurement used scratch scripts (pool tracer, sign-in probe) that are not committed.
